acts.desc: Ira Glass introduces the idea of doing 20 stories in one hour.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: Contributor Starlee Kine talks to actor Tate Donovan about the day he felt he was being exactly the kind of celebrity he'd wanted to be: when suddenly, he was approached by a kid with a camera.
acts.title: Don't I Know You

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Writer and producer Scott Carrier recognizes a woman he sees in a restaurant.
acts.title: No, Of Course I Know You

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Susan Drury talks about "Swap and Shop," a local radio classifieds show that has become a low-tech, personable sort of Ebay.
acts.title: It's Commerce That Brings Us Together

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: From Patty Martin: a one minute, four second vacation on Nantucket Island, involving a lot of waving.
acts.title: The Sound of One Hand Waving

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc: From Vicki Merrick, Eric Kipp, and Jay Allison at Transom: scallops on Martha's Vineyard.
acts.title: The Sound of No Hands Clapping

acts.label: Act Six
acts.desc: From Blunt Youth Radio: a story of a possibly bad "food situation" at the cafeteria in juvenile detention.
acts.title: Reaching Out With Radio

acts.label: Act Seven
acts.desc: Jonathan Goldstein, host of Wiretap, brings us this story about The Penguin as a young man.
acts.title: Up Where the Air Is Clear

acts.label: Act Eight
acts.desc: Two brothers, ages 12 and 13, have very different ideas for their dog's name.
acts.title: The Greatest Dog Name in the World

acts.label: Act Nine
acts.desc: Elaine Boehm overhears a couple in her pet shop, trying to choose a dog collar.
acts.title: Of Dogs and Men

acts.label: Act Ten
acts.desc: A two minute play called “Title,” written and performed by Greg Allen and Heather Riordan of the Chicago group, The Neo-Futurists. It’s part of their long-running show "Too Much Light Makes the Baby Go Blind: 30 Plays in 60 Minutes."

acts.label: Act Eleven
acts.desc: Author David Sedaris on cell phone usage in restrooms.
acts.title: Etiquette Lesson

acts.label: Act Twelve
acts.desc: Brent Runyon reports from the kids' section at the public library.
acts.title: To Tell the Truth

acts.label: Act Thirteen
acts.desc: Catherine and John, two college undergrads, do a babysitting gig together. After the kids are asleep and the two of them get hungry, John doesn't think they should eat any of the food in the house; they settle on a compromise.
acts.title: More Lies

acts.label: Act Fourteen
acts.desc: Mystery and missing flavor at the hot dog plant.
acts.title: Call in Colonel Mustard For Questioning

acts.label: Act Fifteen
acts.desc: Author David Rakoff worked at an advertising agency, and could see exactly where its technology was going.
acts.title: Mister Prediction

acts.label: Act Sixteen
acts.desc: Someone sits next to the printer. You see him forty times a day. What's his name? What does he do?
acts.title: That One Guy at the Office

acts.label: Act Seventeen
acts.desc: Richard Kerry has an impressive ability: he can recreate the sound of a whole swamp.
acts.title: You Can't Choose Your Gift

acts.label: Act Eighteen
acts.desc: Author Chuck Klosterman and his friends make a party game out of comparing television shows to rock bands. They call it "Monkees Equals Monkees."
acts.title: Party Talk

acts.label: Act Nineteen
acts.desc: Every year 1,200 new army cadets arrive at West Point. Once they say a single sentence correctly, they can go to their barracks. But not until then. David Lipsky reports. He's the author of Absolutely American.
acts.title: The Hard Life at the Top

acts.label: Act Twenty
acts.desc: Teenage girls from a detention center perform a song for their parents.
acts.title: The Greatest Moment I Ever Saw On a Stage
